odia: ଗାଁଆଁବାଲା ପଣସ ଖାଇଲେ, ଭଣ୍ଡାରୀ ମୁଣ୍ଡରେ ଅଠା ବୋଳିଲେ
title: Someone else wears the blame
literal_meaning: The villagers ate the jackfruit; they smeared its sticky substance on Bhandari’s head.
explanation: The eaters and the person marked by the sticky residue are different. The headword explicitly explains laying blame or stigma on someone. Our reading follows that transfer: the visible mark is made to point away from those who acted. It is a way to question an accusation, not evidence about any community’s conduct.
meaning_odia: ପଣସ ଖାଇଥିବା ଲୋକ ଓ ମୁଣ୍ଡରେ ଅଠା ବୋଳାଯାଇଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଅଲଗା। ଶବ୍ଦର ଅର୍ଥରେ କାହା ଉପରେ ଦୋଷ ବା କଳଙ୍କ ଦେବା କଥା ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଦାଗଟି ପ୍ରକୃତ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟକାରୀଙ୍କ ବଦଳରେ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷୀ ଦେଖାଉଛି। ଏହା ଅଭିଯୋଗକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବାର ପାଠ, କୌଣସି ସମୁଦାୟର ଆଚରଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: Our reading asks who acted and who was made to carry the visible blame.
odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ପଚାରେ, କାମ କଲା କିଏ ଓ ଦୋଷର ଦାଗ ବୋହିଲା କିଏ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ଦଳର ଭୁଲ ହିସାବ ପାଇଁ କେବଳ ଶେଷରେ ଖାତା ଧରିଥିବା ସଦସ୍ୟଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷ ଦିଆଗଲା। ସେମାନେ ପୁରୁଣା ଲେଖା ମଧ୍ୟ ଯାଞ୍ଚ କଲେ। / A team checks earlier entries before blaming the person currently holding its ledger. This scene is invented.
cultural_context: Bhandari retains the source’s ଭଣ୍ଡାରୀ; this head supplies no occupational or caste identification. A provisional historical bird-and-jackfruit fragment is only a possible parallel, not an imported witness.
